A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniThink and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices. Retained material can be matched across renumbering, relocation and redesigned displays.

before.justification: v2 reports original WildSeek article and outline evaluations, boundary and ablation experiments, human evaluations, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds separate component ablations, evaluator variances, and a human/LLM preference experiment concerning knowledge density.

M1.justification: The information-tree/conceptual-pool procedure, outline construction, article composition and prompt contents remain unchanged. Appendix J explains the existing expansion and stopping decisions; the original algorithm is retained as Algorithm 2. These additions document the procedure without establishing a method revision.

E1.justification: WildSeek coverage is retained. Appendix H adds a narrow synthetic scenario using articles generated from constructed atomic facts to evaluate human and LLM preferences concerning knowledge density.

E2.justification: Figure 6 adds comparisons against two internal variants: OmniThink without the Information Tree and without the Conceptual Pool. External baseline membership remains unchanged. The outline table's RAGo-to-oRAG and DeepThink-to-OmniThink edits correct names while retaining the corresponding scores.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce component-removal controls and a preference protocol holding GPT-4o generation and 500-word article length fixed while varying supplied facts across 20, 30, 40 and 50. Appendix H specifies three human volunteers and three LLM evaluators. Existing benchmark and human-comparison settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.1 adds separate tests of removing tree hierarchy and disabling conceptual-pool reflection. Appendix H adds an experiment testing whether preferences increase with fact density. These substantially extend analysis of the framework's defining components and metric rationale; v2's joint E&R ablation, model-substitution analysis and depth analysis remain.

E5.justification: v2 mentions multiple evaluation rounds without quantitative uncertainty. New Appendix B.3 and Table 4 report variances across three Prometheus evaluation runs using saved checkpoints. This adds evaluator-variability reporting without establishing additional independent article generations or an increase from a previously specified run count.

E6.justification: Main article/outline scores, human-comparison results, URL counts, timings and earlier analysis results are retained. v3 adds component-removal outcomes, evaluation variances and preference scores. For example, Table 7 reports human preferences of 1.0, 2.1, 3.1 and 3.8 for articles supplied with 20, 30, 40 and 50 facts, respectively.

T1.justification: The task definition, tree/pool update equations and Knowledge Density formula remain mathematically unchanged. The additional decision pseudocode clarifies existing operations; no new theorem, proof, formal assumption or mathematical property is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and listed contributions retain the same framework, Knowledge Density metric and knowledge-boundary claims. The model-agnostic integration statement added to the introduction already appeared in v2's conclusion.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the cited reading-cost rationale with a claim of empirical support for KD. Appendix G explains retrieval as adapting to problem difficulty, and B.3 attributes small evaluator variances to Prometheus alignment. Existing boundary interpretations and limitations concerning multimodality and writing style are retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly states WildSeek's 100 items and 24 domains. Appendix J documents node inputs, LLM expansion decisions, empty-output behavior and regular-expression extraction of categories and keywords. Existing generation settings, prompt contents and code/demo links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Table 1 and Appendix G explicitly distinguish OmniThink from STORM and Co-STORM through dynamic retrieval, structured memory and reflection. The reading-cost references by Bovair and Kieras (1991) and Dos Santos and Mookerjee (1993) are removed; the remaining bibliography is retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized edits to author ordering and affiliations, terminology and method labels, removes the introductory quotation, shortens related-work prose and adds acknowledgements. Section 5 gains a dedicated ablation subsection and the appendices gain explanations, while most existing prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2's Figures 3–4 are combined into a redrawn Figure 3, and its three-panel analysis figure becomes v3's five-panel Figure 6. Three tables are added and appendix displays are rearranged. Figure 6 introduces contradictory component captions and legends, while Section 5.3 references incorrect panel letters.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful support missing from v2 through separate component ablations, a controlled preference study concerning KD, evaluator variances and clearer expansion-decision documentation. The gains are limited by the preference study's three human raters and sparse protocol detail, alongside Figure 6's reversed component captions and incorrect panel references.
